summary: This RFC proposes an extension to FTP that stores a file under a unique name chosen by the server, rather than one given by the sender. It acts like the STOR command except for choosing the name.

eli5.summary: Instead of you picking a name for the file you hand over, the receiver picks one that is not already used.

questions: what is the ftp unique named store command
how to upload a file with a unique name in ftp
subtitle: Upload files with server-generated unique names in FTP.

tldr.problem: FTP applications need to upload files to queue directories where the server must pick unique names to avoid collisions, rather than the client specifying names.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 949 adds a new STOU command to FTP that behaves like STOR except the server chooses a unique filename in the current directory and returns it to the client.
tldr.outcome: This solves the problem of applications that manage shared resource pools such as printer daemon queues, fax queues, or job submission directories.

today: RFC 949 is not an Internet Standard; it is Informational. The STOU command is not widely deployed in modern FTP implementations, which have been largely superseded by SFTP, FTPS, and other more modern file transfer protocols.

sections.title: The STOU Command
sections.content:
RFC 949 proposes a new FTP command called STOU (Store Uniquely Named) that extends the File Transfer Protocol. The command works like the existing STOR command, which uploads a file, but instead of the client specifying a filename, the server generates a unique name for the file in the current directory.

This is useful for pool directories such as printer daemon queues, fax queues, and other systems where multiple programs or users need to submit jobs without coordinating on filenames.
sections.eli5: FTP is a way to copy files over the Internet. STOU is like STOR, but instead of you picking the file's name, the server picks a name that is different from all other files there.

sections.title: How STOU Works
sections.content:
When a client sends the STOU command, it opens a data connection and sends file content, just like STOR. The server creates the file with a unique name in the current directory. Unlike other FTP responses, the server must include the actual filename it chose in its response message. The response code is 250 (Transfer Started), and the filename appears in the free-text portion of the response.

The design avoids reopening the existing STOR command, which would break backward compatibility, and instead adds a new command that is easy for FTP implementations to dispatch.
sections.eli5: The server listens to your file data, picks a name that nobody else is using, and tells you what name it picked so you know where to find it.

sections.title: Why This Matters
sections.content: Many network systems use shared queues where programs or users deposit work: printers, fax systems, job schedulers, and other daemons. Without STOU, each client must either coordinate with others to avoid filename conflicts or risk losing data if two submissions arrive with the same name. The RFC notes that STOU would be as reliable as the FTP server's own internal access controls and could be useful wherever the RFC 505 proposal (which suggested a dedicated unique-name directory) was considered.
sections.eli5: When many people want to send in their homework at the same time, they need to make sure nobody sends it under the same name. STOU lets the teacher's mailbox pick a name for each student automatically.
